title: Deferred 2023 year-end financial results and police variance questions
subtitle: Also: 2024 property tax ratios, 2025 budget timetable with 9 a.m. starts, voter turnout and election signs
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee spent most of its meeting on the 2023 year-end financial results. It received the 2023 Plan Update for information. The recommendation to approve the preliminary results and apply the surplus allocation policy was defeated {{vote:m3}}. Some members questioned how the Waterloo Regional Police Service's fourth-quarter variance report was presented. After a recess, the committee waived notice, reconsidered the motion and deferred it to May 7. Written questions are due that Friday. Staff said the delay could affect the audited statements and the provincial financial information return.

The committee recommended 2024 property class tax ratios that match last year's, so there are no tax shifts between classes. It also recommended a 2025 budget timetable in which all Strategic Planning and budget committee meetings start at 9:00 a.m.

Under other business, the committee directed staff to report back on voter engagement efforts. Staff will also update Council on funding for intimate partner violence once it is issued, and review the policy on election signs on regional roads. After the meeting the committee went into closed session on a proposed land acquisition.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended keeping the 2024 ratios the same as 2023, directed staff to prepare the by-laws and rates, and asked that area municipalities be notified {{vote:m2}}.
The committee received the 2023 Plan Update, which reports progress on the Growing with Care Strategic Plan 2023-2027, for information {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: 2023 preliminary financial results and surplus allocation
decisions.detail: The recommendation to approve the preliminary 2023 results and apply the Surplus Allocation Policy was defeated {{vote:m3}}.
The committee waived the notice requirement so the defeated financial results motion could be reconsidered at the same meeting {{vote:m6}}.
The committee agreed to reconsider the defeated recommendations on approving the 2023 financial results and applying the surplus allocation policy {{vote:m7}}.
The committee deferred the reconsidered financial results recommendations to its May 7, 2024 meeting {{vote:m5}}.
The committee amended the 2025 budget timetable so all Strategic Planning and budget committee meetings start at 9:00 a.m. {{vote:m9}}.
The committee recommended the 2025 Plan and Budget review timetable as amended {{vote:m8}}.

debate: One councillor said they could not support the police-related results. They pointed to a change in how wages, salaries and overtime were reported, a larger-than-budgeted transfer to reserves, and the source of funding for a tuition forgiveness program. They also noted that fewer officers were hired than authorized.

Several members said they wanted answers before approving the results, and one said they were not looking for the numbers to change. Others said the committee cannot change the police statements, which the police services board approves, and that the approval is normally a routine step.

Some councillors said the debate was unfairly casting doubt on the police service. Others replied that asking questions is part of due diligence and is not anti-police, and the Chair asked members to avoid personal comments.

Staff said failing to approve the results could delay the audited statements and the financial information return due to the province by the end of May. Staff said no legislated date exists for the statements, and the answers were unlikely to change the numbers.

On the budget timetable, one councillor proposed receiving the police budget a month earlier, but others wanted to hear from the police first. That amendment was withdrawn. Councillors supported 9:00 a.m. starts to allow for long budget days.
